the cloacinogenic plasmid of Clostridium perfringens has a genetic map and that the direction of transcription of its cloacin gene is counter-clockwise.

the genetic analysis of the Clo DF 13 bacteriocinogenic and drug resistance plasmid of Escherichia coli.
the genetic organization of a plasmid which carries a bacteriocin gene.
the isolation of mutants of the bacteriophage lambda, the bacteriocin plasmid CloDF13, the bacteriocins produced by these plasmids and the genes involved in the production of these bacteriocins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Clo DF13 DNA contains at least five genes which can be ordered as follows: A, B, C, G, D.
the Clo DF13 bacteriocinogenic determinant consists of five genes, designated A (cloacine), B, C (both involved in immunity), D and G, which are transcribed from one promoter.
the Clo DF13 DNA is composed of five regions which are transcribed in a counter-clockwise direction and are involved in the synthesis of cloacin.
